$comment: THE DECLARED CREDENTIAL SURFACE OF THIS REPOSITORY'S PUBLISH PATH. scripts/credential-surface.mjs compares this file against .github/workflows/release.yml and against the rotation procedures in RELEASING.md, and fails on any disagreement in either direction. It runs in ci.yml's required `verify` job, so a credential-surface change is refused at merge time, before anyone is asked to approve a deployment. Edit this file in the same commit as the workflow change it describes; that is the whole point of it.
environmentNote: Referencing an environment that does not exist makes GitHub silently auto-create an UNPROTECTED one of that name, so the reference below is evidence that the workflow ASKS for the gate and never evidence that the gate exists. The required reviewer and the main-only branch policy are verified out of band; RELEASING.md carries the API call that sets them and the symptom when they are missing.

documentation.section: Credential rotation, revocation, and compensating actions

credentials.name: GITHUB_OIDC_ID_TOKEN
credentials.tokenClass: A GitHub Actions OIDC ID token, minted on request for a job that grants `id-token: write`, with the audience `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. npm 11.5.1 or later exchanges it, package by package, for a short-lived publish token, and the registry issues one only when the token's claims match that package's trusted publisher: repository cosyte/config, workflow release.yml, environment release. Nothing long-lived exists to issue, store or leak.
credentials.storageNote: Never stored. The runner sets ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN in every step of a job that grants `id-token: write`, and in no other job; the ID token itself is requested by npm inside `npm publish` and is never written to a file, a secret or the job's environment. What can drift is WHICH jobs hold the grant, and the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions below pin that per job. The trusted publisher that makes the exchange succeed lives on npm, per package, and is the owner's to register.

exposures.name: ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL
exposures.note: Set by the runner in every step of the publish job, not by the workflow. The Publish step is the consumer: changesets/action checks for both variables to choose trusted publishing, and npm, run by pnpm under `changeset publish`, requests the ID token with them.

credentials.issuedFormsNote: Empty, and explicit. The ID token is requested by npm and sent only as a request header, which npm's debug log does not record (npm 11.21.0's npm-registry-fetch logs the method, the status and the URL), and the token npm receives in exchange is held in npm's memory for one command and written to no file. The npm token shapes the log collector already redacts stay in release.yml regardless.
credentials.retiredWhen: This repository stops publishing to npm from GitHub Actions, or npm retires trusted publishing. Removing `id-token: write` from the publish job retires nothing: it stops every publish, and the publish preflight refuses before the build when the two variables are missing.

credentials.name: RELEASE_PR_TOKEN
credentials.tokenClass: Fine-grained personal access token scoped to this repository only, with Contents read+write, Pull requests read+write, Metadata read. It does NOT need Workflows write: `pnpm run version` only changes packages/*/package.json, packages/*/CHANGELOG.md and .changeset/.
credentials.storageNote: A repository secret on cosyte/config. Optional by design: without it the version arm still runs, the workflow warns loudly, and the Version Packages PR arrives with zero applicable checks. Its absence must never fail the release closed, because that would take the release path down to protect against a state this repository is already in.

exposures.step: Report whether a version PR would be able to run its checks
exposures.name: HAS_RELEASE_PR_TOKEN

exposures.step: Open or refresh the Version Packages PR
exposures.name: GITHUB_TOKEN

credentials.retiredWhen: GitHub starts workflow runs for events produced by GITHUB_TOKEN, or this repository stops requiring status checks on the Version Packages PR. Neither is expected; until one happens this token is the only thing that makes a Version PR mergeable.

credentials.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
credentials.tokenClass: The installation token GitHub Actions mints per job. It is not issued by a human and cannot be rotated on request; its power is entirely whatever the `permissions:` blocks below grant it.
credentials.storageNote: Never stored. GitHub mints it at job start and revokes it at job end, so there is nothing to rotate and nothing to leak past the run. What CAN drift is its scope, which is why the permissions blocks are declared here rather than left to the workflow alone.

exposures.step: Open or refresh the Version Packages PR
exposures.name: GITHUB_TOKEN

exposures.step: Every bumped package must be published, tagged and released
exposures.name: GH_TOKEN

credentials.permissionsNote: Every job overrides the workflow-level block, which is what keeps `id-token: write` off the two ungated jobs. A NEW job added without a `permissions:` block would inherit the workflow-level grants, `id-token: write` included, and the check refuses that: a job with no block of its own is reported by name.
credentials.retiredWhen: Never, while this repository uses GitHub Actions. What retires is a GRANT: `pull-requests: write` on the version job retires if the Version Packages PR ever stops being opened by this workflow. `id-token: write` on the publish job does not retire: it is what GITHUB_OIDC_ID_TOKEN, the only npm credential, comes from.

settings.name: NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE
settings.purpose: Not a secret, and declared anyway: it is the switch that makes npm provenance self-enabling on the publish step. Deleting it turns provenance off silently on a green run, and nothing else in this repository would notice.

exposures.step: The publish configuration must be one the allow-set permits
exposures.name: NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE
exposures.note: S0081. Effective configuration is a property of a specific process, and this switch is supplied at STEP level, so the allow-check has to carry it or it would be judging a configuration the publish does not have. The allow-set permits `provenance` at `true` and at nothing else, which is what makes deleting this switch from either step a refusal rather than a silent loss of provenance.
